content.title: About
content.content: Spinach is a leafy vegetable belonging to the Amaranthaceae family. Fresh spinach cooked with a small amount of oil retains its bright green color, delicate flavor, and nutritional value. It is commonly used in side dishes, salads, and Asian cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Spinach provides more than 20 vitamins and minerals, including vitamin K, vitamin A, and iron.
Oxalate levels decrease with heat treatment, especially when cooked with oil.
In ancient Rome spinach was considered a "food of the gods" for its vivid color and aroma.
Spinach is cultivated in over 70 countries, with the United States, China, and India being the largest producers.
Leaf color can range from light green to deep purple depending on growing conditions.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for normal blood clotting and supports bone health.

items.title: Source of vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Beta‑carotene, which converts to vitamin A, supports vision and immunity.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from spinach contributes to hemoglobin formation and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from age‑related changes.

items.title: Low‑calorie fiber source
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: High oxalate content
items.content: Oxalates may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Possible drug interactions
items.content: Vitamin K can reduce the effectiveness of anticoagulants such as warfarin.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergy to spinach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spinach cooked with a small amount of oil works well as a side dish, in pastas, omelets, or Asian stir‑fries. Sauté the leaves for 2‑3 minutes until they soften but retain a bright color.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh spinach in the refrigerator in a bag or container with a slight moisture to keep it crisp for up to 5 days. Cooked spinach should be consumed within 2‑3 days, kept in an airtight container.
